catalogue.title: Learn DittoFS
catalogue.lead: How DittoFS works, one part at a time, in plain language. Pick a section; click any underlined term for its definition, and switch language in the top-right corner.

quiz.hint: Pick an answer to see which one is right and why — or press → to move on.
quiz.right: Right. Each option's explanation is under it.
quiz.wrong: Not this one: the right answer is {answer}. Each option's explanation is under it.

introduction.name: Introduction
introduction.blurb: Who uses DittoFS and what they see, the parts inside one node, one write from the client to the bucket and back — and a map of every section that follows.

filesystem-service.name: The filesystem service
filesystem-service.blurb: The one place where every NFS and SMB call is checked — share, permission, open files, quota — in the same order, whichever protocol it came by.

adapters.name: Adapters
adapters.blurb: How NFS and SMB talk to the filesystem: one path for every request and the same rules for every protocol — then what is specific to SMB, and what a Windows client sees when a node goes away.

open-state.name: Open state and locks
open-state.blurb: Who holds a file open, locked or cached, how NFS and SMB share those promises, and what happens to them when a client or the server goes away.

metadata-store.name: The metadata store
metadata-store.blurb: Where DittoFS remembers everything except file bytes: one transactional database, a narrow view for each part, and why busy folders never fight over one key.

engine.name: The engine
engine.blurb: The coordinator that holds no bytes: it decides when each write is acknowledged, uploaded, evicted and fetched back, and in what order.

journal.name: The journal
journal.blurb: Where a write lands first: the local log that keeps every byte safe until it reaches the bucket, then gives the space back.

test-harness.name: The test harness
test-harness.blurb: One command that runs every test suite the same way, on a laptop or in CI, and never counts a test that didn't run as passed.
